- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply downward correction of 5–10% in subsequent periods.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and price drops sharply, model often undercorrects; add 3–7% upward bias to forecast.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent price volatility; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-period moving average) to reduce noise in short-term forecasts.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.6) and price is trending sideways, model tends to drift; anchor forecast to 3–5 day moving average of history.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; reduce first 5–7 days by 3–8% if sentiment is weak or mixed.
- If sentiment turns sharply positive after a dip, model may lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift within 2–3 days.
- When sentiment is high but price is falling, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; add 1–3% downward bias to forecast.
